cohort: 70 healthy, nulliparous pregnant women with singleton pregnancies at 28-32 weeks of gestation
finding: Significant differences in certain personality traits (dependent, passive-aggressive, obsessive-compulsive, antisocial, narcissistic, and borderline) and higher Childbirth Attitudes Questionnaire (CAQ) scores were observed in women who requested cesarean section compared to those who had vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Women who requested cesarean section had significantly higher CAQ scores and were more likely to exhibit certain personality traits, suggesting that these factors may influence mode of delivery preference.
